$schema-note: Image provenance manifest for images DERIVED from retained schematic PDFs by local rasterisation. Kept separate from media/manifest.json so that no pre-existing file is modified; an index owner may merge them.
global_notes: These are NOT photographs and NOT vendor-published images. Each is a crop of a page the vendor published as a vector PDF, rasterised locally at 300 dpi.

pdfimages could not be used: pdfimages -list reports ZERO embedded rasters in every source PDF here. The drawings are vector, so pdftoppm plus a crop is the only route. This is recorded because reaching for pdfimages is the obvious wrong first move.

Copyright in the underlying drawing remains with the vendor named in creator_rightsholder. Licence is UNKNOWN: no licence statement appears in any of the source PDFs. Redistribution status unknown; disposition repository, unstaged pending user review.
Every image is reproducible byte-for-byte from the retained artifact using the recorded generation_command, so none of them is uniquely held here.
Each image exists because it settles a specific documented question; see why_retained.

images.caption: Schematic crop: Grove port J2 (HY-2.0_IIC) with net labels GI and GO
images.alt_text: Schematic detail of a four-pin connector symbol J2, captioned HY-2.0_IIC, whose pin names read IIC_SCL, IIC_SDA, VCC, GND. Two dark-red net labels on the incoming wires read GI and GO, in a serif font where the second character of each is unmistakably a letter I and a letter O rather than a digit. Three ESD diodes D6, D7, D8 sit below.
images.why_retained: Shows that the Grove net names really are the letters GI and GO, which is why every text search for G1 or G2 near this connector failed.

images.caption: Schematic crop: module footprint pin names G1/G2 beside the GI/GO net labels
images.alt_text: Schematic detail showing a yellow module symbol whose printed pin names are G1, G2, G3, G4, G5, G6, G7 in an unmistakable digit glyph, with the dark-red net labels GI, GO, G3, G4, G5, G6, G7 on the wires entering pins 1 to 7.
images.why_retained: The decisive comparison: the same crop contains both the digit glyph (module pin names) and the letter glyph (net labels), proving the GI/GO strings are a vendor typo and that Grove SCL is GPIO1 and SDA is GPIO2.

images.caption: Schematic crop: BMI270 (U7) showing INT1 and INT2 with nothing attached
images.alt_text: Schematic detail of a fourteen-pin IC symbol U7 labelled BMI270. Pins 14 SDX and 13 SCX carry net labels G8 and G9 on wires leaving to the left; pin 1 SDO goes to a pull-up. Pins 4 INT1 and 9 INT2 have bare stubs with no wire, no net label and no connection. Pin 8 VDD goes right through ferrite bead FB7 to +3.3V with C25 and C27.
images.why_retained: Visual confirmation of the negative result that neither BMI270 interrupt line is routed on this board, which removes IMU motion-wake from deep sleep as an option.
